blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Looked-up e-mail address written to the error log) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-privacy-2 (Chat vendor receives phone, birth date and address to greet by name) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence: throw new NotFoundError(`no customer with e-mail ${email}`);
findings.recommendation: Keep the e-mail address out of the error message (for example `throw new NotFoundError("no customer for this e-mail")`). `errorHandler` in src/server.ts logs `err.message` (`logger.error("request failed", { path: req.path, error: err.message })`), so every lookup that finds no customer writes the typed e-mail address to the application log, which has no purpose for it (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation; criterion "No personal data goes to logs").
findings.title: Looked-up e-mail address written to the error log

findings.evidence:
user: {
  id: String(customer.id),
  name: customer.name,
  email: customer.email,
  phone: customer.phone,
  birthDate: customer.birth_date,
  address: customer.address,
},
findings.recommendation: Send the Helply widget only what the stated purpose needs — the proposal says the widget "greets the signed-in customer by name, so that the agent knows who they talk to", which needs `id` and `name` (at most `email`). Drop `phone`, `birthDate` and `address` from `chatWidgetSettings`, and stop selecting them in `customerById` if nothing else uses them. Today `GET /chat/settings` hands the full record to the third-party widget, so every signed-in customer's phone number, birth date and postal address goes to the vendor (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), Art. 25; Art. 28 for the processor).
findings.title: Chat vendor receives phone, birth date and address to greet by name

findings.recommendation: Question for the team — the change starts sending customer data to Helply, but neither the proposal nor the code identifies Helply as a processor (Art. 28 agreement), states the lawful basis for sharing, or says whether the data leaves the EEA (Chapter V). Only the controller can confirm what was decided; record it in the proposal or a decision.
findings.title: Helply processor and possible transfer outside the EEA not identified

findings.evidence: "SELECT id, email, name, phone, birth_date, address FROM customers WHERE lower(email) = lower($1)",
findings.recommendation: The stated purpose is that agents stop asking customers to repeat who they are; confirm which fields agents actually need and return only those from `POST /support/customers/lookup` (birth date and postal address may exceed that purpose, GDPR Art. 5(1)(c)). Depends on support workflows the reviewer could not see.
findings.title: Lookup returns birth date, phone and address to agents
